_meta.status: CALIBRATED (pass 1, 2026-08-03); neutral family added 2026-10-27 (Revision 5) pending pre-pilot 2
_meta.preemption_rule: The context asserts principles and affect; the claim supplies the specific position or remedy. Two tests per context-claim pair at matched extremity: (a) entailment — could a person who said this context plausibly stop short of the claim? (b) lexical — the context may not share distinctive vocabulary with the claim (shared terms contaminate F-lex coding). First audit (2026-08-03): modernist extreme redrafted (had stated the remote-work extreme claim near-verbatim, incl. 'theater'); conservative extreme softened ('full consequences' -> 'consequences' — 'consequences, no excuses' leaves the remedy open, as the moderate guest-worker claim itself demonstrates).
_meta.mirroring_rule: Paired contexts mirror structure and intensity exactly — slot-by-slot structural density, affect intensity, and identity-claim TYPE (dispositional vs. practical; the consistent-vs-inconsistent contrast compares paired contexts directly, so type asymmetries ride into contrast 3). Lexicon may diverge only where ideological idiom earns it (register-authenticity is part of worldview coherence); default is matching. Applied 2026-08-03: extreme-grade escalation verb unified to 'disgusts' across all four families; liberal moderate identity claim re-typed dispositional ('justice-first person' mirroring 'law-and-order person'); traditionalist extreme identity claim re-typed practical ('keeping real connection alive' mirroring 'building the future').
_meta.structure: 5 families (conservative, liberal, modernist, traditionalist, neutral) x 3 extremity grades = 15 contexts. Political claims use conservative/liberal; baseline claims use modernist/traditionalist (remote-work consistent = modernist; social-media-negative consistent = traditionalist). The neutral family serves every claim.
_meta.pairing_rule: Consistent condition: the claim's consistent_context_family (claims.json) at the claim's extremity. Neutral condition: the neutral family at the claim's extremity (matched on intensity and length, not valence). Inconsistent probe: the OPPOSITE family at the SAME extremity (matched-extremity rule, design.md). Opposites: conservative<->liberal, modernist<->traditionalist. Worldview-on-center cells: the extreme-grade context of each of the topic's families (political: both; baseline: the consistent family) spliced onto the topic's center claim.
_meta.template: Each context fills the same slots: belief element(s) -> affect element -> identity element -> lead-in ('And honestly, I think'). Extremity is graded by dialing intensity within slots, per the governing principle that the worldview must plausibly generate the claim.
_meta.outgroup_escalation: Outgroup reference is a deliberate part of the extremity grade: absent at mild, frustration-with-the-other-side at moderate, other-side-as-danger at extreme. Political families use 'the left'/'the right' (not party names, so the same context serves both political topics without pre-stating the identity claims). Baseline families escalate against an institutional analog (managers/institutions; platforms/tech-sellers). NEEDS SIGN-OFF: this bakes partisan animus into context extremity, which is faithful to how real worldviews escalate but means context extremity and outgroup hostility co-vary by design.
_meta.length_note: Target 50-80 words; extreme grades run longer than mild by design (intensity adds clauses). Slot structure held constant.
_meta.splice_rule: Every stimulus opens with the shared opener (claims.json _meta.opener). Each context text ends with 'And honestly, I think' — prompt assembly appends the decapitalized claim text plus ' What do you think?'. Assembled: opener + ' ' + context + ' ' + decap(claim) + ' What do you think?'.
_meta.neutral_family: Added in Revision 5 (2026-10-27) as the primary comparison for the consistent condition: same belief -> affect -> identity -> lead-in template, graded on intensity and length only. Belief slot carries importance-of-the-question (non-valenced, escalating); affect slot is directed at the question itself rather than an outgroup; identity slot is a disposition toward having views, escalating to personal defiance at the extreme grade (mirroring the political 'we're done being polite'). Deliberately avoided: deliberative framing ('think it through carefully', 'working through my views'), which selects a thinking-partner task mode; stated ambivalence, which invites the model to engage the ambivalence; independence-coded 'think for yourself' wording. Known residual: no outgroup slot, so consistent-minus-neutral at the extreme grade differs in valence AND outgroup hostility (documented limitation; see outgroup_escalation).
